claims.statement: URE reported 6,259 refusals of RES connection conditions in 2024, covering almost 42.4 GW of requested capacity, while warning that repeated applications can inflate aggregate capacity.
URE has discussed digitisation, commercial connection arrangements, and cable pooling as ways to improve use of constrained grid capacity.

contrary_evidence: URE explicitly cautions that refused-capacity totals include repeated applications and are not the same as uniquely blocked capacity.
The same refusal statistics demonstrate that acquiring the proposed control point is uncertain rather than automatic.

economics.acquisition_route: Warm introductions from the family installation company, regional landowners, and repeat developer buyers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: by year 6, 10-12 transfers annually at roughly 180000 PLN average revenue and 55% operating margin could support about 1.1-1.2m PLN operating profit; 75% founder ownership plus retained cash could plausibly exceed 5m PLN without counting the same retained earnings twice
economics.founder_time: Initially 3-4 hours/day, with licensed engineering and legal work contracted out
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 55-70% after external grid engineering, legal work, travel, and losses on unsuccessful options
economics.payback: Unvalidated: one successful project transfer could repay the pilot within 12-24 months; failed applications can extend this materially
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 15000-30000 PLN per diligence package plus 100000-300000 PLN or 1-3% of project value on transfer
economics.retention_or_repeat: Developers can buy multiple projects; each site is one-off but the buyer relationship and DSO knowledge repeat

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A private map of DSO outcomes, site load profiles, landowner trust, and a growing portfolio of exclusive project rights
fingerprint.customer: Battery developers, energy traders, and C&I asset owners seeking connection-ready Polish projects
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Parents' renewable installer relationships, landowner referrals, and a small set of repeat storage developers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Data-led site screening, land option, connection application, and packaged project rights; fixed milestones plus transfer success fee
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Developer pays a diligence fee and a larger success or SPV-transfer fee at accepted connection conditions, financing, or acquisition
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A developer needs projects but grid applications are frequently refused and suitable sites are difficult to secure

founder_fit: Leverages the parents' renewable-energy operating network
Can begin regionally with contracted specialists
Does not require a public personal brand
risks: Land-option spend and engineering fees may be lost on refused applications
Assignment, permitting, and energy-law details require specialist counsel
Incumbent developers may already control the most attractive sites

structure.commercial_archetype: Rights-backed project origination with milestone and transfer fees
structure.control_point: Exclusive site options paired with the connection-condition dossier and project SPV
structure.critical_dependency: DSOs must grant usable conditions and the resulting project rights must be assignable or transferable through an SPV

thesis: Originate Polish commercial battery-storage sites by combining time-limited land exclusivity, measured load and feeder evidence, and a professionally prepared DSO connection dossier, then transfer the project company or earn a development fee when a developer funds it. The owned control point is the site-and-connection option, not generic consulting.
title: Grid-Ready Storage Site Option Portfolio
uncertainties: Whether a small entrant can obtain economically useful connection conditions
Whether buyers will pay before permits and financing are complete
The true cycle time and transferability of each DSO's conditions
